::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the MC-4 is and when it was made.
2. Learn its sound, one idea at a time.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Find records it is on.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- The **MC-4 MicroComposer** was released by **Roland** in **1981** (Wikipedia, "Roland MC-4 Microcomposer").
- Music is **typed in as numbers** on a keypad: a number for the pitch, the step time and the gate time (MC-4 manual, pp. 9-10).
- Vince Clarke used it because, as Wikipedia puts it, "The whole theory behind programming with the MC-4 was better timing."
- Its memory is lost when the power goes off, so songs are saved to cassette (manual, pp. 19, 22).

## Its sound

- Keys are **numbered** by counting up the keyboard (manual, p. 9).
- The **time base** is 120 a beat, so a 16th note is **30** (manual, p. 10).
- **CV-1** is the pitch; **CV-2** can go to the filter, the loudness or anything else (manual, p. 11).
- It has **four channels** (manual, p. 11).

## Famous records

Named in Wikipedia, "Roland MC-4 Microcomposer":

- Yazoo, *Upstairs at Eric's* (1982) (Vince Clarke)
- Erasure, *Chorus* (1991) (Vince Clarke)
- also used by Kraftwerk, Depeche Mode, The Human League and Yellow Magic Orchestra

## Check yourself

Click an answer. You will see at once if it is right. Nothing is saved or sent.

```{=html}
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>How do you put music into the MC-4?</b></p><ul><li>Type numbers on a keypad</li><li>Sing into it</li><li>Draw with a pen</li><li>Play a guitar</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual pp. 9-10.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>With a time base of 120, a 16th note is…</b></p><ul><li>30</li><li>120</li><li>16</li><li>60</li></ul><p class="ik-why">120 ÷ 4 = 30.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>CV-1 controls…</b></p><ul><li>The pitch</li><li>The tempo</li><li>The lights</li><li>The tape</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual p. 11.</p></div>
<div class="ik-q" data-a="0"><p><b>What happens to its memory when the power goes off?</b></p><ul><li>It is lost, so save to cassette</li><li>It is kept for ever</li><li>It plays louder</li><li>It prints</li></ul><p class="ik-why">Manual pp. 19, 22.</p></div>
```
